mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market weakness, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following a sustained GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals robust economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following a sustained RSAFS increase.
